record.paper_title: Aspects of Nonabelian Group Based Cryptography: A Survey and Open Problems
record.original_question: What is the computational complexity of the twisted search conjugacy problem in polycyclic groups?

evidence.quote: 4. What is the complexity of the twisted search conjugacy problem in polycyclic groups?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a polycyclic group, given by a finite polycyclic presentation (so that elements are represented by collected normal words). For an endomorphism φ : G → G, two elements u, v ∈ G are said to be φ-twisted conjugate if there exists x ∈ G such that v = x^{-1} u φ(x). The twisted search conjugacy problem is: given as input a polycyclic presentation of G, an endomorphism φ : G → G (specified by the images of the generators), and two elements u, v ∈ G that are known (or promised) to be φ-twisted conjugate, compute an element x ∈ G such that v = x^{-1} u φ(x).

Determine the computational complexity of this problem as a function of the input size (the lengths of the words representing u, v, the images φ(g_i), and the size of the presentation). In particular, decide whether it admits a polynomial-time algorithm, or establish hardness (e.g., NP-hardness) for some family of polycyclic groups.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work provides decidability results and practical algorithms for the twisted conjugacy problem in polycyclic and virtually polycyclic groups (e.g., Tertooy 2020, 2025), and shows the (uniform) ordinary conjugacy problem can be NP-complete on certain polycyclic families. However, a precise complexity classification of the twisted search conjugacy problem in polycyclic groups does not appear to have been established; subsequent surveys (e.g., the 2016 polycyclic-cryptography status survey) continue to list it among open questions.

status_evidence.title: Algorithms for twisted conjugacy classes of polycyclic-by-finite groups
status_evidence.snippet: Practical algorithms deciding twisted conjugacy under finite Reidemeister coincidence number conditions in polycyclic-by-finite groups.
status_evidence.claim: Decidability and algorithms exist but no tight complexity bound is given.

status_evidence.title: A family of polycyclic groups over which the uniform conjugacy problem is NP-complete
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs polycyclic groups whose uniform conjugacy problem is NP-complete via subset sum.
status_evidence.claim: Related (untwisted) conjugacy problem can be NP-complete; twisted version's complexity not pinned down.

status_evidence.title: The Status of Polycyclic Group-Based Cryptography: A Survey and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems including the complexity of the twisted (search) conjugacy problem in polycyclic groups.
status_evidence.claim: The complexity of the twisted search conjugacy problem in polycyclic groups remains an open problem.
